title: High Society and the mirroring of chords
summary: Randolph denies Luis Russell wrote High Society and explains his chord mirroring with a pivotal chord, later found in Miller's New Harmonic Devices, which New York loved.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: According to this reissue, they said that Luis Russell did that arrangement, though they say that you did all the arrangements recorded in Chicago. But they do say that Luis Russell did the 'High Society' arrangement.
I know, because you had talked to me about that, and we --

Not High -- no. No, 'High Society' was a jammed-up thing. That's where I did something new, mirroring of chords, and I did that through sheer of hearing it, and some years later, after making the arrangements, I was studying New Harmonic Devices By Miller. Did you ever read that? New Harmonic Devices by Miller.
And I found out what I was doing, I was doing a mirroring of chords.
A mirror, that's something. Now, for instance, now, this is a C chord. This is a C chord. (Piano playing.) See?
You used extensions of the chords.
That's right, you -- to really put it point blank, your first chord would be used as a pivotal chord.
-- a pivotal chord, and your other chord, or the chord that you mirror would be dissonant against that because you're going out of the key.
You go out of the key against that. And that's where I got that (musical sounds), and I'd get chords [ ], and then Louis come in (musical sounds), see?
He'd taper it off, because I'd give him the tone to make his gliss 4h horn.
See, the tone there -- I wanted him to make that gliss. And it came out pretty well. We hit to New York with that thing, and they went wild over it.
I guess that's the first time they ever heard anything like that.
Yeah. Well, it sounds a little like what the guys were doing a few years later, in bebop.
In the flat five's and the 13ths and so forth.
Yes, uh-huh. Only one thing, I did this with the whole band -- the whole -- (musical sounds), I did this with the whole outfit.
